{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = 'data/sales.csv'
sales = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Parse revenue: remove commas and convert to float
sales['revenue'] = sales['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Drop QA orders with revenue 999999.99
sales_clean = sales[~sales['revenue'].isin([999999.99])]

# Drop refunded orders (only completed orders count)
sales_final = sales_clean[sales_clean['status'] == 'completed']

# Compute conversion rate for each channel within each segment
conversion_by_channel_segment = sales_final.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['converted'].mean().unstack()

# Also compute average revenue by channel within each segment
revenue_by_channel_segment = sales_final.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['revenue'].mean().unstack()

# Extract conversion rates for each channel by segment using .loc
email_conv = conversion_by_channel_segment.loc['email']
paid_search_conv = conversion_by_channel_segment.loc['paid_search']

# Compute the difference in conversion rate between channels, within each segment
conversion_diff = email_conv - paid_search_conv

# Similarly for revenue
email_rev = revenue_by_channel_segment.loc['email']
paid_search_rev = revenue_by_channel_segment.loc['paid_search']

# Compute the difference in average revenue
revenue_diff = email_rev - paid_search_rev

# Now, compute the actual average revenue for paid_search in each segment
# We already have paid_search_rev, but we need to print it explicitly
print('Average revenue for paid_search by segment:')
print(paid_search_rev)

# Also print the actual average revenue for email
print('\nAverage revenue for email by segment:')
print(email_rev)

# Now, print the differences again
print('\nConversion rate difference (email - paid_search) by segment:')
print(conversion_diff)
print('\nAverage revenue difference (email - paid_search) by segment:')
print(revenue_diff)"}
